title: I'm having trouble because UseVBOs isn't showing up in the graphics options.
content:

title: Game Inspired Character Outfit — Recreated in Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/69f213cd187f4c0284ba3e11354e4c07INVISIB_19.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/23f5f0319f4b4022bb76e1f0681a751bINVISIB_19.png)Invisible Women Inspired Outfit — Marvelous Designer Project

While playing a game, I came across a character skin that immediately caught my attention because of its **bold colors, retro style, and strong character personality**. The design felt unique and stylish, and I wanted to challenge myself by recreating a similar outfit using **Marvelous Designer**.

This project became an opportunity to explore how a **game-inspired costume** could be translated into a garment created entirely through digital pattern making and cloth simulation.

![7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/7fb2b8776aac4e388b6a4f5364ff9f15Screenshot%20%28505%29.png)

* * *

### Reference and Inspiration

The main inspiration for this outfit came from Marvel Rivals **game character skin**. What stood out to me the most was the combination of:

  * Bright pink color palette

  * Retro fashion elements

  * Futuristic character styling




The design balances **playful fashion with a confident hero-like presence** , which made it an interesting challenge to recreate.

### Building the Outfit in Marvelous Designer

The outfit was constructed step by step inside Marvelous Designer using pattern-based garment creation.

The process started with the **base pants and top** , carefully fitted to the avatar to establish a clean silhouette. Once the foundation was working correctly, additional pieces were layered to build the final look.

Key garment pieces include:

  * A **structured corset-style top** with panel segmentation

  * **High-waisted pants** with curved seam lines

  * A **short cropped jacket** to add structure and contrast

  * A **scarf accessory** to introduce movement to the design




Each piece was simulated and adjusted to maintain a natural garment flow.

![64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/64ee918a73394cb6afdda3267fefd00bScreenshot%20%28534%29.png)

### Details and Character Elements

To capture the personality of the original inspiration, several stylistic elements were incorporated:

  * A decorative **belt with circular details and emblem**

  * Retro-inspired **sunglasses**

  * Flowing lower pant sections that soften the silhouette




These elements help create a design that feels **stylish, playful, and character-driven**.

![f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/f5f69c5af6474e519f90fba738533238INVISIB_19.png)

![606c628ae36340e886989db582082cca](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/a134284c3e064f41b169c1c1dece5a9a/images/606c628ae36340e886989db582082ccaINVISIB_21.png)

### Final Thoughts

This project was mainly a **practice and exploration piece** , inspired by a game skin that I enjoyed while playing. Recreating it in Marvelous Designer helped me better understand **pattern construction, garment layering, and digital clothing simulation**.

It was a fun challenge to translate a **stylized game costume into a simulated garment** , and it allowed me to experiment with both **fashion design and character outfit creation**.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: This is awesome! I want to jump into The Sims right now and put this on my Sim.
Reply 1: That’s such a compliment, thanks😍
content_description: Explore the creative journey of translating a bold, game-inspired character outfit into a stylish digital garment using Marvelous Designer, showcasing innovative pattern construction and cloth simulation techniques.

title: Stylized Character: Character Creator, Marvelous Designer and Blender Workflow
content:
### ![fc393d7faa274eb9b1c3db6b8b89df53](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/fc393d7faa274eb9b1c3db6b8b89df53still4.jpg)**Melis Caner / Melniverse**

Hi, I’m Melis Caner, a 3D Generalist and filmmaker. My lifelong love for drawing, fashion, dancing, and acting now comes together in 3D animation, blending all my passions into one art form.  
<https://www.instagram.com/melniverse/>

* * *

Lately, I’ve been obsessed with Jackson Wang- Cruel music video. I really like where the Dancer Queen character moves the boulders from the ground. So I wanted to create a similar scene, but in my style. Time: 2:00

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rhy7_Y15FrI?si=wO4yRN21uU4x6ela?start=120

To start with the character I want to dress I used Character Creator 5. I start by using the new HD Stylized base model. It's easy to use and totally customizable. ![38eca3fc32434402b16e53274500124f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/38eca3fc32434402b16e53274500124fmel-05-1536x864.webp)  
I captured my motion with the Rokoko motion capture suit. 

I added facial animation with the Digital Soul pack in iClone. This basically drags and drops the selected expression, then applies it to my character.  
![c6c1d9b76ca7442786a37beacc5e78fc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/c6c1d9b76ca7442786a37beacc5e78fcmel-06-2-1536x864.webp)  
**3D Cloth Customization and Cloth Simulation**

For the outfit, I downloaded a 3D suit on CLO Connect, uploaded by MONA.   
<https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/350811/info>  
On top of it, I designed the cropped sleeves of the clothing, and then simulated everything in Marvelous Designer.  
![1f14ce0b5573425a82264856890e5e4a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/1f14ce0b5573425a82264856890e5e4amel-09-1536x898.webp)

Finally, I built the scene in Blender using the 3D Scans that scanned by Blendreams in the ancient city in Turkey. <https://www.instagram.com/blendreams/>  
![c24cee7ab4584524b824e8c6a69f3c61](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/c24cee7ab4584524b824e8c6a69f3c61mel-10-1536x907.webp)![4b1904f865974d2ebe8db0e4e8fc2afb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/013a7ea375ef416daf1a7cc8eed706ed/images/4b1904f865974d2ebe8db0e4e8fc2afbmel-12.jpg)  
You can see the full breakdown video and the final result here:

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HzqBfl-cvPY?si=frV-CjrfPZxc_fAz

title: ExportUSDがうまく使えません。
content:
pythonAPIでUSDファイルを書き出そうと思っています。

しかし、UI上から設定したusdとpythonAPIから設定して書き出したusdが異なってしまいます。  
UI上から設定できる副資材（stitchやプロップなど）のオンオフもPython上からだとうまくいきません。

  
以下PC環境

  * OS Windows 11 Pro (64ビット) - Build 10.0.26200

  * CPU intel Core Ultra 9 285K (24コア / 24スレッド) 

  * GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 (VRAM 4GB*) + Intel Graphics (内蔵) 




メモリ 約64GB   


# クラッシュについて

  
また、ExportUSDコマンドはファイルパスを指定して実行するとMDがクラッシュします。その為、ファイルパスの引数指定なしで実行したのち、所定の位置にコピーするような処理を入れています。

  
PythonAPIドキュメントのUSDに関する情報も乏しく、情報頂けると助かります。

* * *

以下使用しているPythonスクリプトです。

"""Marvelous Designer 内で直接実行する USD エクスポートスクリプト  
"""  
  
import export_api  
import import_api  
import utility_api  
import ApiTypes  
import os  
import json  
import shutil  
  
# exec() 実行時は **file** が未定義のため、スクリプト自身のディレクトリを  
# inspect で取得してパスを解決する  
try:  
_SCRIPT_ DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))  
except NameError:  
import inspect  
_SCRIPT_ DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(inspect.getfile(inspect.currentframe())))  
  
# ======================================================================  
# ロガー — cp932 回避のため print + 最後にまとめて UTF-8 書き出し  
# ======================================================================  
_LOG_PATH = os.path.join(_SCRIPT_DIR, "Aru_md_batch.log")  
_log_lines = []  
  
def log(level, msg):  
import datetime  
line = f"{[datetime.datetime.now](http://datetime.datetime.now)():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S} [{level}] {msg}"  
_log_ lines.append(line)  
print(line)  
  
def log_flush():  
with open(_LOG_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
f.write("\n".join(_log_lines))  
  
# ======================================================================  
# プログレスバー  
# ======================================================================  
def progress(title, pct):  
"""MD のプログレスバーを更新する。pct: 0〜100"""  
utility_api.SetProgressW(title, int(pct))  
utility_api.Refresh3DWindow() # UIイベントを強制処理してバーを即時描画  
  
# ======================================================================  
# CONFIG  
# ======================================================================  
_JSON_PATH = os.path.join(_SCRIPT_DIR, "Aru_md_batch.json")  
  
def _load_ config():  
if os.path.exists(_JSON_PATH):  
with open(_JSON_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:  
cfg = json.load(f)  
log("INFO", f"JSON を読み込みました: {_JSON_PATH}")  
return cfg  
return {  
"zprj_path" : "",  
"pose_usd_path" : "",  
"export_usd_path": "",  
"simulate_steps" : 120,  
"quality" : 1,  
"start_frame" : 0,  
"end_frame" : 120,  
}  
  
# ======================================================================  
# オプション構築  
# ======================================================================  
def _build_ export_option():  
opt = ApiTypes.ImportExportOption()  
opt.bExportGarment = True # ガーメント本体のみ（isSelectAllPatternsChecked=true相当）  
opt.bExportAvatar = False  
opt.bExportLight = False  
opt.bExportFabric = False  
opt.bIncludeHiddenObject = False  
opt.bSingleObject = True #統合したオブジェクトとして  
opt.bThin = True #薄いシェイプでエクスポート  
opt.bUnifiedUVCoordinates = True #UVを統合  
opt.bCreateUnifiedTexture = True #テクスチャを統合して出力  
opt.bIncludeInnerShape = True  
opt.bIncludeAvatarShape = False  
opt.bSaveInZip = False  
opt.bMetaData = True  
opt.scale = .1 # cmに合わせてスケールダウン  
opt.bCreateClothCacheAnimation = True  
opt.bCreateAvatarCacheAnimation = False  
return opt  
  
def _build_ usd_option():  
opt = ApiTypes.ExportUSDOption()  
opt.m_upAxis = 0 # プリセット: usdUpAxis=0 (Z-up)  
opt.m_metersPerUnit = 0.001 # cm 単位  
opt.m_bAssignGarment = True  
opt.m_bAssignAvatar = False  
opt.m_bAssignSceneNProp = False # isSelectAllSceneAndPropsChecked=false相当  
opt.m_garmentPrimPath = "/Garment"  
opt.m_bExportSimulationData = True # includeGarmentSimulationData=false相当  
opt.m_bExportStrandData = False # includeFurStrandData=false相当  
return opt  
  
# ======================================================================  
# メイン  
# ======================================================================  
def main():  
log("INFO", "===== Aru_md_batch 開始 =====")  
cfg = _load_ config()  
log("INFO", f"CONFIG: {cfg}")  
  
  
zprj_path = cfg.get("zprj_path", "").strip()  
pose_usd_path = cfg.get("pose_usd_path", "").strip()  
export_usd_path = os.path.normpath(cfg.get("export_usd_path", "").strip())  
simulate_steps = int(cfg.get("simulate_steps", 120))  
quality = int(cfg.get("quality", 1))  
start_frame = float(cfg.get("start_frame", 0))  
end_frame = float(cfg.get("end_frame", 120))  
  
if not zprj_path:  
log("ERROR", "'zprj_path' が設定されていません。")  
log_flush(); return  
if not export_usd_path:  
log("ERROR", "'export_usd_path' が設定されていません。")  
log_flush(); return  
  
export_dir = os.path.dirname(export_usd_path)  
if export_dir:  
os.makedirs(export_dir, exist_ok=True)  
  
# ---- プロジェクト読み込み ----  
log("INFO", f"プロジェクトを開く: {zprj_path}")  
try:  
import_option = ApiTypes.ImportZPRJOption()  
import_option.bLoadGarment = True  
import_option.bLoadAvatar = False  
result = import_api.ImportZprjW(zprj_path, import_option)  
log("DEBUG", f"ImportZprjW 戻り値: {result}")  
except Exception as e:  
log("WARN", f"ImportZprjW 例外: {e} — ImportFileW にフォールバック")  
result = import_api.ImportFileW(zprj_path)  
log("DEBUG", f"ImportFileW 戻り値: {result}")  
if not result:  
log("ERROR", "プロジェクトの読み込みに失敗しました")  
log_flush(); return  
log("INFO", "プロジェクトを開きました")  
  
# ---- アバター読み込み ----  
if pose_usd_path:  
log("INFO", f"ポーズファイルを読み込む: {pose_usd_path}")  
ext = os.path.splitext(pose_usd_path)[1].lower()  
loaded = False  
try:  
if ext in (".usd", ".usda", ".usdc", ".usdz"):  
result = import_api.ImportFileW(pose_usd_path)  
elif ext == ".avt":  
result = import_api.ImportAvatar(pose_usd_path, ApiTypes.ImportExportOption())  
elif ext == ".abc":  
result = import_api.ImportAlembic(pose_usd_path, ApiTypes.ImportAlembicOption())  
else:  
result = import_api.ImportFileW(pose_usd_path)  
log("DEBUG", f"アバター読み込み戻り値: {result}")  
loaded = bool(result)  
except Exception as e:  
log("WARN", f"アバター読み込み例外: {e}")  
log("INFO", "アバター読み込み完了" if loaded else "アバター読み込み失敗（続行）")  
else:  
log("INFO", "pose_usd_path 未指定 — スキップ")  
  
# ---- シミュレーション（落ち着かせ） ----  
log("INFO", f"シミュレーション品質: quality={quality}")  
try:  
utility_api.SetSimulationQuality(quality, 0)  
except Exception as e:  
log("WARN", f"SetSimulationQuality 例外: {e}")  
  
log("INFO", f"シミュレーション開始 ({simulate_steps} steps) ...")  
try:  
utility_api.Simulate(simulate_steps)  
log("INFO", "シミュレーション完了")  
except Exception as e:  
log("ERROR", f"Simulate 例外: {e}")  
log_flush(); return  
  
# ---- アニメーション録画（キャッシュ生成） ----  
# Simulate() はポーズに落ち着かせるだけ。  
# アニメーションのフレームキャッシュを生成するには  
# RunAnimationRecording() で全フレームを再生・焼き込む必要がある。  
total_frames = int(end_frame \- start_frame)  
log("INFO", f"アニメーション録画: frame {start_frame} → {end_frame}")  
try:  
utility_api.SetStartAnimationFrame(start_frame)  
utility_api.SetEndAnimationFrame(end_frame)  
utility_api.CreateProgressBar()  
progress(f"アニメーション録画中... (0/{total_frames}frames)", 0)  
utility_api.RunAnimationRecording(start_frame, end_frame)  
progress(f"アニメーション録画完了 ({total_frames}frames)", 100)  
utility_api.DeleteProgressBar(False)  
log("INFO", "アニメーション録画完了")  
except Exception as e:  
log("ERROR", f"RunAnimationRecording 例外: {e}")  
utility_api.DeleteProgressBar(True)  
log_flush(); return  
  
# ---- USD エクスポート（一時フォルダ → コピー）----  
# Top-stitch はAPIフラグで除外できないため、  
# エクスポート前に非表示化 + bIncludeHiddenObject=False で対処する  
# 6:Threads(Top-stitch含む), 7:Pins を非表示に  
_HIDE_ OPTIONS = [6, 7]  
log("INFO", "Top-stitch / Pins を非表示に設定")  
for opt_i in _HIDE_ OPTIONS:  
try:  
utility_api.SetGarmentDisplayProperties(opt_i, False)  
except Exception as e:  
log("WARN", f"SetGarmentDisplayProperties({opt_i}, False) 例外: {e}")  
  
log("INFO", f"USD エクスポート開始 → 最終出力先: {export_usd_path}")  
try:  
exp_opt = _build_ export_option()  
usd_opt = _build_ usd_option()  
log("INFO", "ExportUSD（一時フォルダ）実行中...")  
tmp_paths = export_api.ExportUSD(exp_opt, usd_opt)  
log("INFO", f"一時フォルダ出力: {tmp_paths}")  
except Exception as e:  
log("ERROR", f"ExportUSD 例外: {e}")  
log_flush(); return  
  
if not tmp_paths:  
log("ERROR", "ExportUSD の戻り値が空です")  
log_flush(); return  
  
# 書き出されたファイルをコピー  
src = tmp_paths[0]  
src_ext = os.path.splitext(src)[1] # 例: .usda / .usd  
dst_base = os.path.splitext(export_usd_path)[0]  
dst = dst_base \+ src_ext  
try:  
shutil.copy2(src, dst)  
log("INFO", f"コピー完了: {src} -> {dst}")  
except Exception as e:  
log("ERROR", f"コピー失敗: {e}")  
log_flush(); return  
  
# 表示を元に戻す  
log("INFO", "Top-stitch / Pins の表示を復元")  
for opt_i in _HIDE_ OPTIONS:  
try:  
utility_api.SetGarmentDisplayProperties(opt_i, True)  
except Exception as e:  
log("WARN", f"SetGarmentDisplayProperties({opt_i}, True) 例外: {e}")  
  
  
  
log("INFO", "===== Aru_md_batch 完了 =====")  
log_flush()  
  
  
main()

title: Marvelous Designer for Motion Graphics: Seamless Integration with C4D
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/883ac020cb3d45a3973bbab96029ccdd/images/b656dbd45e804715beb52bc660ce88ec%E1%84%8A%E1%85%A5%E1%86%B7%E1%84%82%E1%85%A6%E1%84%8B%E1%85%B5%E1%86%AF.png)

# **Motion Graphic Designer, Hyeonpyo Lee**

[**Behance**](https://www.behance.net/gallery/242975231/Porter-Brand-Promotion-Film)  
[**Instagram**](https://www.instagram.com/hyeon_pyo_/)

# **Could you provide a short introduction and describe your current professional focus?**

Hi, I’m Hyunpyo Lee, a 3D motion graphic designer. I specialize in articulating brand philosophies by weaving visual metaphors into compelling stories. My current creative direction involves transcending literal descriptions of product structures to reconstruct them as a unique world-building experience.

# **Project Introduction: What is the concept and creative intent behind the ‘Porter Brand Promotion Film’?**

The foundation of this project is the core philosophy of the Japanese bag brand, Yoshida Porter: “Heart and Soul in Every Stitch.”

A bag is an object brought to life through the harmonious assembly of diverse parts and structures. I believed that reinterpreting these functional elements as a living, natural ecosystem could give birth to a compelling narrative.

To realize this vision, I constructed a world where the bag’s components—zippers, clips, fabrics, and D-rings—are transformed into living organisms or elements of nature. For example, zippers are depicted as bioluminescent fireflies navigating the dark, fabrics soar through the sky like birds, and metal clips glide through the water like fish.

By portraying these distinct entities living in their respective environments before eventually converging into a single bag, I aimed to metaphorically express the brand's intricate structure and meticulous craftsmanship. Rather than focusing on a direct product showcase, this brand film was designed to visually capture the "journey" of the elements that together define the essence of the bag.

# **What was the decisive factor in choosing Marvelous Designer, and what specific challenges (e.g., garment simulation, realism) did it help you solve in this project?**

The primary reason was to accurately capture the natural physical properties and structural integrity of fabric during the bag-making process.

For the scenes where the bag is being constructed, I wanted the patterns and sewing structures to be represented just as they are in real-world garment manufacturing. It was crucial that the process—being cut from patterns and stitched together—looked convincing and authentic, rather than appearing as a simply modeled piece of cloth.

**![1e73bf7480aa4e0c9a9cf4b9a7ba6574](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/883ac020cb3d45a3973bbab96029ccdd/images/1e73bf7480aa4e0c9a9cf4b9a7ba657401.png)![8834b94026c845728c43a35b3de60998](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202603/883ac020cb3d45a3973bbab96029ccdd/images/8834b94026c845728c43a35b3de6099802.png)**Because Marvelous Designer allows for the direct implementation of this pattern-based construction, it was exceptionally effective for:

  * **Bag Pattern Creation**

  * **Fabric Simulation**

  * **Representation of Sewing Structures**




As a result, I was able to achieve natural wrinkles, tension, and intricate stitching details that would have been difficult to create through conventional modeling alone. This significantly enhanced both the realism and the overall quality of the production scenes.

# **Technical Workflow: How did Marvelous Designer integrate into your overall pipeline (including other tools)? Do you have any tips or precautions regarding data export?**

The overall pipeline was structured as follows:

**Marvelous Designer → Cinema 4D → Octane Render → After Effects**

I began by creating the bag patterns and configuring the sewing structures within Marvelous Designer, completing the primary form through fabric simulation. The results were then exported as **Alembic (.abc)** files and imported into Cinema 4D. There, I integrated hardware parts and other 3D elements before proceeding with animation and lighting.

During the export process, I found a few key points to be essential:

First, **managing mesh density is crucial.** Using the simulation results as-is can lead to excessively high polygon counts. Therefore, it was necessary to optimize the mesh density to ensure smooth performance in subsequent stages of the pipeline.

Second, **properly managing the "Layer" settings in Simulation Properties is vital.** In Marvelous Designer, designs often involve overlapping patterns or polygons. Depending on the Layer values, you may encounter issues like mesh penetration or clipping during simulation. Strategically assigning Layer values—carefully considering which pattern sits on top and which sits beneath—was fundamental to achieving a stable and clean simulation.

# **What do you feel are Marvelous Designer's distinct advantages compared to other 3D tools? Was there a specific feature that impressed you most during your work?**

In my view, the greatest strength is the seamless synergy between pattern-based creation and physical simulation.

While many conventional 3D tools rely on sculpting fabric shapes or adjusting them through post-simulation, Marvelous Designer centers the entire workflow on designing actual patterns and sewing them together—mirroring real-world garment manufacturing. The **Sewing** feature, in particular, allowed me to intuitively configure connections and stitching structures. This was incredibly effective for projects like bags or clothing, where the integrity of the construction and the sewing method are paramount.

I was also deeply impressed by the instantaneous feedback loop when modifying patterns. Even a subtle adjustment to a pattern's length or curvature naturally transforms the entire silhouette. This organic connection, where design and simulation coexist in a single, fluid workflow, was truly fascinating.

#   
**What practical advice would you give to motion graphic designers who are considering adopting Marvelous Designer or to those who are just starting out and facing challenges?**

**** I believe Marvelous Designer is much more than just a tool for simulating cloth; it becomes far more powerful when approached with an understanding of patterns and structure.

Instead of treating it like a typical 3D modeling tool, I recommend starting by creating simple patterns yourself. It is crucial to go through the process of understanding how these flat patterns transform into three-dimensional forms. I also had my own fears about learning a new tool, but I found that many features are so intuitive that I was able to adapt much faster than expected. I encourage beginners not to feel overwhelmed, but to dive in and explore the possibilities.

Another method I highly recommend is referring to real-world pattern data. For instance, **CLO-SET**[**Connect**](https://connect.clo-set.com/store) shares a vast array of garment patterns and technical drawings. Analyzing these pattern structures and applying them to your own work will significantly deepen your understanding of the software.

As projects involving materials with specific physical properties—such as clothing, fabrics, and bags—continue to grow within the motion graphics field, I believe Marvelous Designer is an incredibly valuable tool that allows for the simultaneous expression of both physical properties and intricate structure.
